page: Google Cloud Platform c4d-highcpu-8 is an x86_64 architecture server instance belonging to the c4d server family. It features 8 dedicated virtual central processing units (vCPUs) paired with 15.0 gigabytes of system memory. This configuration yields a memory-to-core ratio of 1.88 gigabytes per vCPU, indicating a hardware profile optimized primarily for compute-heavy workloads rather than memory-intensive tasks.

The instance does not include local storage, requiring external block storage solutions for data persistence. It also lacks integrated graphics processing units (GPUs) and does not provide complimentary public IPv4 addresses. These design choices reflect a streamlined resource allocation model focused on raw CPU execution. The low memory density per core represents a clear tradeoff, making the instance less suitable for large in-memory databases or massive datasets, but highly efficient for tasks where CPU execution speed is the primary bottleneck.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the c4d-highcpu-8 offers a dense allocation of dedicated compute resources relative to its memory footprint, allowing users to pay primarily for processing power without the overhead of unused RAM. This resource balance is designed for workloads such as batch processing, web serving, distributed compute nodes, and continuous integration and continuous delivery (CI/CD) pipelines where processing demands outweigh memory capacity.
